analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of ClusterService.swift (911–1536) and the bounded change orientation. These excerpts are outside the complete changed-line ranges and do not independently establish a regression. Existing interactions include worker-digest-triggered replanning under the command lock (950–1014), coordinator approval fetching and synchronized replacement after draining parts (1024–1138), approval-expiry stopping and local-serving fallback (1328–1409), pending cache reclamation (1365–1368), child environment separation and supervision (1425–1464), and bounded SIGTERM shutdown (1508–1525). Relevant contracts include A-001/A-003 confidentiality, A-016 and T-052/T-053 serving authorization, T-041 cache isolation/storage, and A-018 availability. Local-serving fallback and file reads shown here are BASE behavior, not new findings.
The patch orientation changes responder visibility, replaces cable-check timestamps with listener/pairing checks, and adds a Listening dependency to internal composition. Integration must examine the changed listener implementation and its callers, particularly ClusterService.swift HEAD 337–420: verify that pairing changes revoke stale responders/control listeners, that cable moves preserve peer authentication, and that concurrent listener replacement cannot retain stale control authority or disrupt draining/leases. The supplied partial patch and BASE-only surrounding source cannot resolve those security-sensitive contracts. No new encryption, attestation, billing, or cache-policy change is demonstrated in these units; missing HEAD implementation is a coverage limit rather than evidence of safety.
